name: East Of The Sun And West Of The Moon

pages.caption: Once upon a time there was a poor husbandman who had many children and little to give them in the way either of food or clothing.
pages.description: [A poor husbandman and many children in a humble cottage]
pages.scene: A poor husbandman and many children in a humble cottage

pages.caption: They were all pretty, but the prettiest of all was the youngest daughter, who was so beautiful that there were no bounds to her beauty.
pages.description: [A beautiful youngest daughter among her siblings]
pages.scene: A beautiful youngest daughter among her siblings

pages.caption: So once it was late on a Thursday evening in autumn, and wild weather outside, terribly dark, and raining so heavily and blowing so hard that the walls of the cottage shook again.
pages.description: [A dark autumn night with violent wind and rain]
pages.scene: A dark autumn night with violent wind and rain

pages.caption: They were all sitting together by the fireside, each of them busy with something or other, when suddenly some one rapped three times against the window-pane.
pages.description: [A family gathered around a warm fireside]
pages.scene: A family gathered around a warm fireside

pages.caption: The man went out to see what could be the matter, and when he got out there stood a great big white bear.
pages.description: [A great white bear standing outside the door]
pages.scene: A great white bear standing outside the door

pages.caption: Good-evening to you, said the White Bear.
pages.description: [The white bear speaking to the man]
pages.scene: The white bear speaking to the man

pages.caption: Good-evening, said the man.
pages.scene: The man standing before the bear

pages.caption: Will you give me your youngest daughter, said the White Bear; if you will, you shall be as rich as you are now poor.
pages.scene: The white bear making an offer

pages.caption: Truly the man would have had no objection to be rich, but he thought to himself, I must first ask my daughter about this.
pages.scene: The man listening thoughtfully

pages.caption: So he went in and told them that there was a great white bear outside who had faithfully promised to make them all rich if he might but have the youngest daughter.
pages.description: [The man speaking to his family indoors]
pages.scene: The man speaking to his family indoors

pages.caption: She said no, and would not hear of it.
pages.scene: The youngest daughter refusing

pages.caption: So the man went out again, and settled with the White Bear that he should come again next Thursday evening, and get her answer.
pages.description: [The man negotiating with the white bear outside]
pages.scene: The man negotiating with the white bear outside

pages.caption: Then the man persuaded her, and talked so much to her about the wealth that they would have, and what a good thing it would be for herself, that at last she made up her mind to go.
pages.scene: The man persuading his daughter

pages.caption: And washed and mended all her rags, made herself as smart as she could, and held herself in readiness to set out.
pages.description: [The girl washing and mending her clothes]
pages.scene: The girl washing and mending her clothes

pages.caption: Little enough had she to take away with her.
pages.scene: The girl with a small bundle

pages.caption: Next Thursday evening the White Bear came to fetch her.
pages.description: [The white bear arriving on Thursday evening]
pages.scene: The white bear arriving on Thursday evening

pages.caption: She seated herself on his back with her bundle, and thus they departed.
pages.description: [The girl seated on the white bear's back]
pages.scene: The girl seated on the white bear's back

pages.caption: When they had gone a great part of the way, the White Bear said, Are you afraid?
pages.description: [The white bear and girl riding across a vast landscape]
pages.scene: The white bear and girl riding across a vast landscape

pages.caption: No, that I am not, said she.
pages.scene: The girl riding confidently

pages.caption: Keep tight hold of my fur, and then there is no danger, said he.
pages.scene: The white bear speaking gently

pages.caption: And thus she rode far, far away, until they came to a great mountain.
pages.description: [The pair riding far across mountains and valleys]
pages.scene: The pair riding far across mountains and valleys

pages.caption: Then the White Bear knocked on it, and a door opened.
pages.description: [The white bear knocking on the mountain]
pages.scene: The white bear knocking on the mountain

pages.caption: And they went into a castle where there were many brilliantly lighted rooms which shone with gold and silver.
pages.description: [A magnificent castle of gold and silver]
pages.scene: A magnificent castle of gold and silver

pages.caption: Likewise a large hall in which there was a well-spread table, and it was so magnificent that it would be hard to make anyone understand how splendid it was.
pages.description: [A great hall with a well-spread table]
pages.scene: A great hall with a well-spread table

pages.caption: The White Bear gave her a silver bell, and told her that when she needed anything she had but to ring this bell, and what she wants would appear.
pages.description: [The white bear handing a silver bell to the girl]
pages.scene: The white bear handing a silver bell to the girl

pages.caption: So after she had eaten, and night was drawing near, she grew sleepy after her journey, and thought she would like to go to bed. She rang the bell.
pages.scene: The girl ringing the silver bell

pages.caption: And scarcely had she touched it before she found herself in a chamber where a bed stood ready made for her, which was as pretty as anyone could wish to sleep in.
pages.description: [A beautiful bedroom with silk pillows and gold curtains]
pages.scene: A beautiful bedroom with silk pillows and gold curtains

pages.caption: It had pillows of silk, and curtains of silk fringed with gold, and everything that was in the room was of gold or silver.
pages.scene: Silk pillows and golden furnishings

pages.caption: But when she had lain down and put out the light a man came and lay down beside her.
pages.description: [The girl lying in the bed as darkness falls]
pages.scene: The girl lying in the bed as darkness falls

pages.caption: And behold it was the White Bear, who cast off the form of a beast during the night.
pages.description: [The white bear form casting off at night]
pages.scene: The white bear form casting off at night

pages.caption: She never saw him, however, for he always came after she had put out her light, and went away before daylight appeared.
pages.scene: The girl sleeping unaware

pages.caption: So all went well and happily for a time, but then she began to be very sad and sorrowful, for all day long she had to go about alone.
pages.description: [The girl alone in the castle, looking sad]
pages.scene: The girl alone in the castle, looking sad

pages.caption: And she did so wish to go home to her father and mother and brothers and sisters.
pages.description: [The girl gazing out the castle window]
pages.scene: The girl gazing out the castle window

pages.caption: Then the White Bear asked what it was that she wanted, and she told him that it was so dull there in the mountain.
pages.description: [The white bear asking what troubles her]
pages.scene: The white bear asking what troubles her

pages.caption: And that she had to go about all alone, and that in her parents house at home there were all her brothers and sisters, and it was because she could not go to them that she was so sorrowful.
pages.scene: The girl speaking sadly

pages.caption: There might be a cure for that, said the White Bear, if you would but promise me never to talk with your mother alone, but only when the others are there too.
pages.description: [The white bear giving a stern warning]
pages.scene: The white bear giving a stern warning

pages.caption: For she will take hold of your hand, he said, and will want to lead you into a room to talk with you alone; but that you must by no means do, or you will bring great misery on both of us.
pages.scene: The white bear continuing his warning

pages.caption: So one Sunday the White Bear came and said that they could now set out to see her father and mother, and they journeyed thither, she sitting on his back.
pages.description: [The white bear and girl riding to her parents home]
pages.scene: The white bear and girl riding to her parents home

pages.caption: And they went a long, long way, and it took a long, long time; but at last they came to a large white farmhouse, and her brothers and sisters were running about outside it, playing.
pages.description: [A large white farmhouse with children playing]
pages.scene: A large white farmhouse with children playing

pages.caption: Your parents dwell here now, said the White Bear; but do not forget what I said to you, or you will do much harm both to yourself and me.
pages.scene: The white bear speaking before departure

pages.caption: No, indeed, said she, I shall never forget.
pages.scene: The girl promising

pages.caption: And as soon as she was at home the White Bear turned round and went back again.
pages.scene: The white bear turning to leave

pages.caption: There were such rejoicings when she went in to her parents that it seemed as if they would never come to an end.
pages.scene: The family rejoicing together

pages.caption: Now they had everything that they wanted, and everything was as good as it could be.
pages.description: [The family with plenty in their home]
pages.scene: The family with plenty in their home

pages.caption: They all asked her how she was getting on where she was. All was well with her too, she said.
pages.scene: The family asking about her life

pages.caption: But in the afternoon, after they had dined at midday, all happened just as the White Bear had said. Her mother wanted to talk with her alone in her own chamber.
pages.scene: The mother drawing her daughter aside

pages.caption: But she remembered what the White Bear had said, and would on no account go.
pages.scene: The girl remembering the warning

pages.caption: What we have to say can be said at any time, she answered. But somehow or other her mother at last persuaded her.
pages.scene: The mother persuading her daughter

pages.caption: And she was forced to tell the whole story. So she told how every night a man came and lay down beside her when the lights were all put out.
pages.scene: The girl telling her secret

pages.caption: And how she never saw him, because he always went away before it grew light in the morning.
pages.scene: The girl continuing her tale

pages.caption: And how she continually went about in sadness, thinking how happy she would be if she could but see him.
pages.scene: The girl expressing her longing

pages.caption: Oh! cried the mother, in horror, you are very likely sleeping with a troll!
pages.scene: The mother horrified

pages.caption: But I will teach you a way to see him. You shall have a bit of one of my candles, which you can take away with you hidden in your breast.
pages.scene: The mother offering a candle

pages.caption: Look at him with that when he is asleep, but take care not to let any tallow drop upon him.
pages.scene: The mother giving final instructions

pages.caption: So she took the candle, and hid it in her breast, and when evening drew near the White Bear came to fetch her away.
pages.description: [The girl hiding the candle in her breast]
pages.scene: The girl hiding the candle in her breast

pages.caption: When they had gone some distance on their way, the White Bear asked her if everything had not happened just as he had foretold.
pages.description: [The white bear questioning the girl on the journey]
pages.scene: The white bear questioning the girl on the journey

pages.caption: And she could not but own that it had. Then, if you have done what your mother wished, said he, you have brought great misery on both of us.
pages.scene: The girl admitting the truth

pages.caption: No, she said, I have not done anything at all.
pages.scene: The girl reassuring the bear

pages.caption: So when she had reached home and had gone to bed it was just the same as it had been before, and a man came and lay down beside her.
pages.description: [The girl lying in bed at night]
pages.scene: The girl lying in bed at night

pages.caption: And late at night, when she could hear that he was sleeping, she got up and kindled a light.
pages.description: [The girl rising quietly in the dark]
pages.scene: The girl rising quietly in the dark

pages.caption: Lit her candle, let her light shine on him, and saw him, and he was the handsomest prince that eyes had ever beheld.
pages.scene: The candle illuminating a handsome prince

pages.caption: And she loved him so much that it seemed to her that she must die if she did not kiss him that very moment.
pages.description: [The girl gazing at the sleeping prince]
pages.scene: The girl gazing at the sleeping prince

pages.caption: So she did kiss him.
pages.description: [The girl leaning in to kiss the prince]
pages.scene: The girl leaning in to kiss the prince

pages.caption: But while she was doing it she let three drops of hot tallow fall upon his shirt.
pages.description: [Three drops of tallow falling on his shirt]
pages.scene: Three drops of tallow falling on his shirt

pages.caption: And he awoke. What have you done now? said he; you have brought misery on both of us.
pages.scene: The prince awakening

pages.caption: If you had but held out for the space of one year I should have been free. I have a step-mother who has bewitched me so that I am a white bear by day and a man by night.
pages.scene: The prince explaining his curse

pages.caption: But now all is at an end between you and me, and I must leave you, and go to her.
pages.scene: The prince departing in sorrow

pages.caption: She lives in a castle which lies east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.scene: The prince describing the castle

pages.caption: And there too is a princess with a nose which is three ells long, and she now is the one whom I must marry.
pages.description: [The prince speaking of the troll princess]
pages.scene: The prince speaking of the troll princess

pages.caption: She wept and lamented, but all in vain, for go he must.
pages.scene: The girl weeping

pages.caption: Then she asked him if she could not go with him. But no, that could not be.
pages.scene: The girl asking to follow

pages.caption: Can you tell me the way then, and I will seek you, that I may surely be allowed to do!
pages.scene: The girl determined

pages.caption: Yes, you may do that, said he; but there is no way thither.
pages.scene: The prince answering

pages.caption: It lies east of the sun and west of the moon, and never would you find your way there.
pages.scene: The prince speaking his final words

pages.caption: When she awoke in the morning both the Prince and the castle were gone, and she was lying on a small green patch in the midst of a dark, thick wood.
pages.description: [The girl waking alone on a small green patch]
pages.scene: The girl waking alone on a small green patch

pages.caption: By her side lay the self-same bundle of rags which she had brought with her from her own home.
pages.scene: The bundle of rags beside her

pages.caption: So when she had rubbed the sleep out of her eyes, and wept till she was weary, she set out on her way.
pages.scene: The girl weeping in the forest

pages.caption: And thus she walked for many and many a long day, until at last she came to a great mountain.
pages.scene: The girl walking many long days

pages.caption: Outside it an aged woman was sitting, playing with a golden apple.
pages.description: [An old woman sitting outside the mountain playing with a golden apple]
pages.scene: An old woman sitting outside the mountain playing with a golden apple

pages.caption: The girl asked her if she knew the way to the Prince who lived with his stepmother in the castle which lay east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.scene: The girl asking the old woman

pages.caption: How do you happen to know about him? inquired the old woman; maybe you are she who ought to have had him.
pages.scene: The old woman responding

pages.caption: Yes, indeed, I am, she said. So it is you, then? said the old woman.
pages.scene: The girl confirming

pages.caption: I know nothing about him but that he dwells in a castle which is east of the sun and west of the moon. But you shall have the loan of my horse.
pages.scene: The old woman offering her horse

pages.caption: And then you can ride on it to an old woman who is a neighbor of mine: perhaps she can tell you about him.
pages.scene: The old woman giving instructions

pages.caption: When you have got there you must just strike the horse beneath the left ear and bid it go home again; but you may take the golden apple with you.
pages.description: [The old woman handing the golden apple]
pages.scene: The old woman handing the golden apple

pages.caption: So the girl seated herself on the horse, and rode for a long, long way.
pages.description: [The girl riding the horse across the land]
pages.scene: The girl riding the horse across the land

pages.caption: And at last she came to the mountain, where an aged woman was sitting outside with a gold carding-comb.
pages.description: [The second old woman with a gold carding-comb]
pages.scene: The second old woman with a gold carding-comb

pages.caption: The girl asked her if she knew the way to the castle which lay east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.scene: The girl asking again

pages.caption: But she said what the first old woman had said: I know nothing about it, but that it is east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.scene: The second old woman responding

pages.caption: But you shall have the loan of my horse to an old woman who lives the nearest to me: perhaps she may know where the castle is.
pages.description: [The second old woman offering her horse]
pages.scene: The second old woman offering her horse

pages.caption: Then she gave her the gold carding-comb, for it might, perhaps, be of use to her, she said.
pages.description: [The second old woman giving the carding-comb]
pages.scene: The second old woman giving the carding-comb

pages.caption: So the girl seated herself on the horse, and rode a wearisome long way onward again.
pages.scene: The girl riding onward

pages.caption: And after a very long time she came to a great mountain, where an aged woman was sitting, spinning at a golden spinning-wheel.
pages.description: [The third old woman with a golden spinning-wheel]
pages.scene: The third old woman with a golden spinning-wheel

pages.caption: Of this woman, too, she inquired if she knew the way to the Prince, and where to find the castle which lay east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.description: [The girl asking the third old woman]
pages.scene: The girl asking the third old woman

pages.caption: But it was only the same thing once again. Maybe it was you who should have had the Prince, said the old woman.
pages.scene: The third old woman speaking

pages.caption: Yes, indeed, I should have been the one, said the girl.
pages.scene: The girl confirming her purpose

pages.caption: But this old crone knew the way no better than the others. It was east of the sun and west of the moon, she knew that.
pages.scene: The third old woman giving directions

pages.caption: But you may have the loan of my horse, and I think you had better ride to the East Wind, and ask him.
pages.description: [The third old woman suggesting the East Wind]
pages.scene: The third old woman suggesting the East Wind

pages.caption: And then she gave her the golden spinning-wheel, saying, Perhaps you may find that you have a use for it.
pages.description: [The third old woman giving the spinning-wheel]
pages.scene: The third old woman giving the spinning-wheel

pages.caption: The girl had to ride for a great many days, and for a long and wearisome time, before she got there.
pages.scene: The girl riding for many days

pages.caption: But at last she did arrive, and then she asked the East Wind if he could tell her the way to the Prince.
pages.description: [The East Wind as a gentle breeze]
pages.scene: The East Wind as a gentle breeze

pages.caption: Well, said the East Wind, I have heard tell of the Prince, and of his castle, but I do not know the way to it.
pages.scene: The East Wind speaking

pages.caption: But, if you like, I will go with you to my brother the West Wind: he may know that, for he is much stronger than I am.
pages.scene: The East Wind offering help

pages.caption: You may sit on my back, and then I can carry you there.
pages.description: [The girl seated on the East Wind]
pages.scene: The girl seated on the East Wind

pages.caption: So she seated herself on his back, and they did go so swiftly!
pages.description: [The East Wind and girl flying swiftly]
pages.scene: The East Wind and girl flying swiftly

pages.caption: When they got there, the East Wind went in and said that the girl whom he had brought was the one who ought to have had the Prince.
pages.scene: The West Wind greeting them

pages.caption: No, said the West Wind; so far as that have I never blown.
pages.scene: The West Wind responding

pages.caption: But if you like I will go with you to the South Wind, for he is much stronger than either of us.
pages.scene: The West Wind offering to help

pages.caption: You may seat yourself on my back, and then I will carry you to him.
pages.description: [The girl riding with the West Wind]
pages.scene: The girl riding with the West Wind

pages.caption: So she did this, and journeyed to the South Wind, neither was she very long on the way.
pages.description: [The South Wind as a warm gust]
pages.scene: The South Wind as a warm gust

pages.caption: Oh, indeed! said the South Wind, is that she? I have wandered about a great deal in my time, but I have never blown so far as that.
pages.scene: The South Wind speaking

pages.caption: But if you like I will go with you to my brother, the North Wind; he is the oldest and strongest of all of us.
pages.scene: The South Wind offering help

pages.caption: You may sit upon my back, and then I will carry you there.
pages.description: [The girl riding with the South Wind]
pages.scene: The girl riding with the South Wind

pages.caption: When they came near the North Wind's dwelling, he was so wild and frantic that they felt cold gusts a long while before they got there.
pages.scene: The North Wind's cold dwelling approaching

pages.caption: What do you want? he roared out from afar, and they froze as they heard.
pages.scene: The North Wind roaring

pages.caption: It is I, and this is she who should have had the Prince who lives in the castle which lies east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.scene: The South Wind explaining

pages.caption: Yes, said the North Wind, I know where it is. I once blew an aspen leaf there.
pages.scene: The North Wind responding

pages.caption: But I was so tired that for many days afterward I was not able to blow at all. However, if you really are anxious to go there, I will take you on my back.
pages.scene: The North Wind warning

pages.caption: Get there I must, said she; and if there is any way of going I will; and I have no fear, no matter how fast you go.
pages.scene: The girl expressing determination

pages.caption: Very well then, said the North Wind; but you must sleep here to-night, for if we are ever to get there we must have the day before us.
pages.scene: The North Wind advising rest

pages.caption: The North Wind woke her betimes next morning, and puffed himself up, and made himself so big and so strong that it was frightful to see him.
pages.description: [The North Wind waking her at dawn]
pages.scene: The North Wind waking her at dawn

pages.caption: And away they went, high up through the air, as if they would not stop until they had reached the very end of the world.
pages.description: [The North Wind and girl flying high above the world]
pages.scene: The North Wind and girl flying high above the world

pages.caption: Down below there was such a storm! It blew down woods and houses, and when they were above the sea the ships were wrecked by hundreds.
pages.scene: Storm below as they fly

pages.caption: And thus they tore on and on, and a long time went by, and still they were above the sea, and the North Wind grew tired.
pages.scene: The North Wind growing tired

pages.caption: And more tired, and at last so utterly weary that he was scarcely able to blow any longer, and he sank and sank, lower and lower.
pages.scene: The North Wind sinking lower

pages.caption: Until at last he went so low that the waves dashed against the heels of the poor girl he was carrying.
pages.scene: Waves dashing against the girls heels

pages.caption: Art thou afraid? said the North Wind.
pages.scene: The North Wind asking

pages.caption: I have no fear, said she; and it was true.
pages.scene: The girl fearless

pages.caption: But there was just enough strength left in the North Wind to enable him to throw her on to the shore, immediately under the windows of a castle.
pages.description: [The North Wind casting her to shore]
pages.scene: The North Wind casting her to shore

pages.caption: Which lay east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.description: [The castle lying east of the sun and west of the moon]
pages.scene: The castle lying east of the sun and west of the moon

pages.caption: But then he was so weary and worn out that he was forced to rest for several days before he could go to his own home again.
pages.scene: The North Wind exhausted

pages.caption: Next morning she sat down beneath the walls of the castle to play with the golden apple.
pages.description: [The girl sitting beneath the castle walls playing with the golden apple]
pages.scene: The girl sitting beneath the castle walls playing with the golden apple

pages.caption: And the first person she saw was the maiden with the long nose, who was to have the Prince.
pages.description: [The troll princess with a long nose at the window]
pages.scene: The troll princess with a long nose at the window

pages.caption: How much do you want for that gold apple of yours, girl? said she, opening the window.
pages.scene: The troll princess asking

pages.caption: It cant be bought either for gold or money, answered the girl.
pages.scene: The girl answering

pages.caption: If it cannot be bought either for gold or money, what will buy it? You may say what you please, said the Princess.
pages.scene: The troll princess pressing further

pages.caption: Well, if I may go to the Prince who is here, and be with him to-night, you shall have it, said the girl.
pages.scene: The girl making her offer

pages.caption: You may do that, said the Princess, for she had made up her mind what she would do.
pages.scene: The troll princess agreeing

pages.caption: So the Princess got the golden apple.
pages.description: [The troll princess taking the golden apple]
pages.scene: The troll princess taking the golden apple

pages.caption: But when the girl went up to the Princes apartment that night he was asleep, for the Princess had so contrived it.
pages.description: [The girl entering the princes chamber at night]
pages.scene: The girl entering the princes chamber at night

pages.caption: The poor girl called to him, and shook him, and between whiles she wept.
pages.description: [The girl calling to the sleeping prince]
pages.scene: The girl calling to the sleeping prince

pages.caption: But she could not wake him.
pages.scene: The prince sleeping soundly

pages.caption: In the morning, as soon as day dawned, in came the Princess with the long nose, and drove her out again.
pages.description: [The troll princess driving her out at dawn]
pages.scene: The troll princess driving her out at dawn

pages.caption: In the daytime she sat down once more beneath the windows of the castle, and began to card with her golden carding-comb.
pages.description: [The girl sitting beneath the windows with the carding-comb]
pages.scene: The girl sitting beneath the windows with the carding-comb

pages.caption: And then all happened as it had happened before. The Princess asked her what she wanted for it.
pages.description: [The troll princess asking for the comb]
pages.scene: The troll princess asking for the comb

pages.caption: And she replied that it was not for sale, either for gold or money, but that if she could get leave to go to the Prince she should have it.
pages.scene: The girl repeating her offer

pages.caption: But when she went up to the Princes room he was again asleep.
pages.description: [The girl entering the princes room again]
pages.scene: The girl entering the princes room again

pages.caption: And let her call him, or shake him, or weep as she would, he still slept on, and she could not put any life in him.
pages.scene: The girl weeping and shaking him

pages.caption: When daylight came in the morning, the Princess with the long nose came too, and once more drove her away.
pages.description: [The troll princess driving her away again]
pages.scene: The troll princess driving her away again

pages.caption: When day had quite come, the girl seated herself under the castle windows, to spin with her golden spinning-wheel.
pages.scene: The girl spinning beneath the windows

pages.caption: And the Princess with the long nose wanted to have that also. So she opened the window, and asked what she would take for it.
pages.scene: The troll princess wanting the spinning-wheel

pages.caption: The girl said what she had said on each of the former occasions. It was not for sale either for gold or for money, but if she could get leave to go to the Prince she should have it.
pages.description: [The girl making the same offer again]
pages.scene: The girl making the same offer again

pages.caption: Yes, said the Princess, I will gladly consent to that.
pages.scene: The troll princess agreeing again

pages.caption: But in that place there were some Christian folk who had been carried off, and they had been sitting in the chamber which was next to that of the Prince.
pages.scene: Christian prisoners in the next chamber

pages.caption: And had heard how a woman had been in there who had wept and called on him two nights running, and they told the Prince of this.
pages.scene: The prisoners telling the prince

pages.caption: So that evening, when the Princess came once more with her sleeping-drink, he pretended to drink, but threw it away behind him.
pages.description: [The prince pouring out the sleeping drink]
pages.scene: The prince pouring out the sleeping drink

pages.caption: For he suspected that it was a sleeping-drink.
pages.scene: The prince suspicious

pages.caption: So, when the girl went into the Princes room this time he was awake, and she had to tell him how she had come there.
pages.description: [The girl entering the princes room and finding him awake]
pages.scene: The girl entering the princes room and finding him awake

pages.caption: You have come just in time, said the Prince, for I should have been married to-morrow.
pages.scene: The prince speaking joyfully

pages.caption: But I will not have the long-nosed Princess, and you alone can save me.
pages.scene: The prince declaring his love

pages.caption: I will say that I want to see what my bride can do, and bid her wash the shirt which has the three drops of tallow on it.
pages.scene: The prince devising a plan

pages.caption: This she will consent to do, for she does not know that it is you who let them fall on it.
pages.scene: The prince explaining

pages.caption: But no one can wash them out but one born of Christian folk: it cannot be done by one of a pack of trolls.
pages.scene: The prince continuing

pages.caption: And then I will say that no one shall ever be my bride but the woman who can do this, and I know that you can.
pages.scene: The prince making his vow

pages.caption: There was great joy and gladness between them all that night.
pages.scene: The girl and prince rejoicing together

pages.caption: But the next day, when the wedding was to take place, the Prince said, I must see what my bride can do.
pages.scene: The wedding preparations beginning

pages.caption: That you may do, said the stepmother.
pages.scene: The stepmother agreeing

pages.caption: I have a fine shirt which I want to wear as my wedding shirt, but three drops of tallow have got upon it which I want to have washed off.
pages.scene: The prince presenting the shirt

pages.caption: And I have vowed to marry no one but the woman who is able to do it. If she cannot do that, she is not worth having.
pages.scene: The prince making his vow

pages.caption: Well, that was a very small matter, they thought, and agreed to do it.
pages.scene: The trolls confident

pages.caption: The Princess with the long nose began to wash as well as she could.
pages.scene: The troll princess washing the shirt

pages.caption: But the more she washed and rubbed, the larger the spots grew.
pages.scene: The stains growing worse

pages.caption: Ah! you cant wash at all, said the old troll-hag, who was her mother. Give it to me.
pages.scene: The old troll-hag taking the shirt

pages.caption: But she too had not had the shirt very long in her hands before it looked worse still, and the more she washed it and rubbed it, the larger and blacker grew the spots.
pages.scene: The old troll-hag failing

pages.caption: So the other trolls had to come and wash, but the more they did, the blacker and uglier grew the shirt.
pages.scene: Other trolls trying to wash

pages.caption: Until at length it was as black as if it had been up the chimney.
pages.description: [The shirt as black as chimney soot]
pages.scene: The shirt as black as chimney soot

pages.caption: Oh, cried the Prince, not one of you is good for anything at all!
pages.scene: The prince calling out

pages.caption: There is a beggar-girl sitting outside the window, and Ill be bound that she can wash better than any of you! Come in, you girl there!
pages.scene: The prince summoning the girl

pages.caption: So she came in. Can you wash this shirt clean? he cried.
pages.scene: The girl entering

pages.caption: Oh! I dont know, she said; but I will try.
pages.scene: The girl modestly answering

pages.caption: And no sooner had she taken the shirt and dipped it in the water than it was white as driven snow.
pages.description: [The girl dipping the shirt in water]
pages.scene: The girl dipping the shirt in water

pages.caption: And even whiter than that.
pages.scene: The shirt perfectly white

pages.caption: I will marry you, said the Prince.
pages.scene: The prince declaring his choice

pages.caption: Then the old troll-hag flew into such a rage that she burst.
pages.scene: The old troll-hag bursting with rage

pages.caption: And the Princess with the long nose and all the little trolls must have burst too, for they have never been heard of since.
pages.scene: The trolls vanishing

pages.caption: The Prince and his bride set free all the Christian folk who were imprisoned there.
pages.description: [The prince and girl freeing the prisoners]
pages.scene: The prince and girl freeing the prisoners

pages.caption: And took away with them all the gold and silver that they could carry.
pages.scene: The couple departing with treasure

pages.caption: And moved far away from the castle which lay east of the sun and west of the moon.
pages.description: [The couple leaving the castle far behind]
pages.scene: The couple leaving the castle far behind
